name: Health Canada Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-282)
summary: Canada's federal regulations, made under the Food and Drugs Act, governing the sale, import, and advertising of medical devices, including software as a medical device. Devices are classified by risk from Class I to Class IV, and Health Canada licenses devices and the establishments that import or distribute them, and oversees post-market safety.
keyRequirements: Classify each device by risk (Class I lowest to Class IV highest); a device that fits two classes takes the higher
Hold a medical device licence before importing or selling a Class II, III, or IV device
Hold a medical device establishment licence to import or distribute devices, unless an exemption applies
Report incidents involving death or serious deterioration in health within 10 days, and incidents that could cause it if they recurred within 30 days
Notify the Minister within 24 hours of deciding to recall a device, and report on the recall's results
Report serious risks identified in foreign actions within 72 hours, and prepare annual or biennial summary reports for Class II to IV devices
Address cybersecurity in pre-market applications for connected devices, per Health Canada guidance
penalties: Under the Food and Drugs Act: on indictment, fines up to $5,000,000 CAD and up to 2 years imprisonment; on summary conviction, up to $250,000 CAD and 6 months for a first offence and $500,000 CAD and 18 months thereafter. Knowingly or recklessly causing a serious risk of injury carries a fine at the court's discretion and up to 5 years imprisonment. Each day of a continuing offence is a separate offence.
